title: Three pasts; the 'line' past for -ar verbs: -aba

cards.title: Three pasts: have, line, dot
cards.body: All the English ways fit into three Spanish pasts: 'I have eaten' (haber); a line in the past (I was eating, I used to eat, I would eat every week as a child); and a dot in the past (I ate, finished).

cards.title: Recap: haber + -ado / -ido
cards.body: The -ado / -ido form never changes; only haber does. Only the futures add onto the full 'to' form.

examples.en: I haven't been able to eat.

cards.title: habría + -ido
cards.body: Divide it up: first habría, then salido. Don't translate it as one block.

examples.en: I wouldn't have been able to go out.

cards.title: The line past: -ar → -aba
cards.body: For ongoing past (was …ing, used to …), take off -ar and add -aba. Like 'would', the I form is the same as he/she/it/formal you. We form: -ábamos (stress stays on the same a).

examples.en: I / he was speaking, used to speak
you were / they were / we were speaking

cards.title: esperaba
cards.body: Lo / la also mean formal you.

examples.en: We were waiting for you guys.

cards.title: intentaba
cards.body: Spanish usually avoids the preposition (encontrármelo). Use para mí only to emphasise.

examples.en: They were trying to find it.
They were trying to find it for me.

practice.en: I haven't been able to eat.
We were waiting for you guys.
They were trying to find it.
They were trying to find it for me.
